commands_run: ./run_in_docker.sh 'mvn -q -B -DskipTests compile && mvn -q -B org.apache.maven.plugins:maven-dependency-plugin:3.1.1:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile=/tmp/pov_cp.txt -Dmdep.includeScope=test && mkdir -p /tmp/pov_build && javac -cp "target/classes:$(cat /tmp/pov_cp.txt)" -d /tmp/pov_build .security-pipeline/pov/PathTraversalPovTest.java && java -cp "/tmp/pov_build:target/classes:$(cat /tmp/pov_cp.txt)" org.junit.runner.JUnitCore PathTraversalPovTest'
output_json.diff_review: patch_only.diff touches only src/main/java/spark/resource/{AbstractResourceHandler,ExternalResourceHandler,ClassPathResourceHandler}.java plus two test files; it does not touch the POV file (.security-pipeline/pov/PathTraversalPovTest.java is untouched/untracked, not part of patch_only.diff). The new isPathUnderBase() helper normalizes both base and candidate with the existing StringUtils.cleanPath() utility, adds consistent leading/trailing slash boundaries (avoiding a naive startsWith bypass like '/public-evil' matching '/public'), and requires the candidate to remain within the base. It is invoked immediately after each addPaths() concatenation (both the primary resolution and the welcome-file branch) in both handler classes, returning null (treated as not-found) on containment failure — matching the CWE-022 alert's guidance that the check must occur after concatenation/resolution, and covering both the ExternalResourceHandler/ExternalResource and ClassPathResourceHandler/ClassPathResource sink families named in the alert traces. The change is minimal, additive (early-return guard only), does not alter behavior for legitimate in-root paths, and does not modify or weaken the POV. Two new regression tests per handler (backslash and plain '../' traversal) were added and are appropriate, not a removal of coverage.
output_json.pov_result: Independently reran the exact pov_command via the docker wrapper against the patched worktree: JUnit run failed (exit 1) with AssertionError 'Vulnerable behavior expected: ExternalResourceHandler resolved a resource for a ..\ traversal request path instead of rejecting it' — confirming the ExternalResourceHandler now returns null for the crafted backslash-traversal servlet path and the out-of-root secret file is no longer disclosed. This matches the orchestrator's reported pov_after_patch result (exit 1) and contrasts with pov_before_patch (exit 0, vulnerable).
output_json.regression_result: Independently reran the targeted regression command (ExternalResourceHandlerTest, ClassPathResourceHandlerTest, UriPathTest, AbstractResourceTest) via the docker wrapper: 27/27 tests passed, 0 failures/errors — matching the orchestrator's regression_2 log. The orchestrator's full `mvn -B test` run (regression_3) also reports 295/295 passing with BUILD SUCCESS, and `mvn -B -DskipTests package` succeeds. No regressions observed.
output_json.summary: The patch adds a shared containment check (AbstractResourceHandler.isPathUnderBase) applied after path concatenation in both ExternalResourceHandler.getResource(String) and ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource(String) (including their welcome-file re-resolution branches), rejecting any resolved path that normalizes outside the configured base resource root. This directly closes the CWE-022 gap where UriPath.canonical() ignored backslash-based '..' traversal and StringUtils.cleanPath() normalized but never rejected excess '..' segments. Independently reran the POV and targeted regressions via the docker wrapper: POV now fails (vulnerability no longer reproduces) and all existing resource-handler tests plus the full test suite reported by the orchestrator pass.
